title: The Upanishads
author: Swami Paramananda (trans)
description: The Upanishads, translated and commented on by Swami Paramananda (1884-1940) of the Ramakrishna Order, founder of the Vedanta Centre in Boston and Ananda Ashrama in California (Volume I, 1919). Aimed at Western readers, it gives clear English translations of principal Upanishads, among them the Isa, Katha and Kena Upanishads, each with an introduction and running commentary. The Isa opens with seeing the Lord in all things; the Katha tells of the boy Nachiketas who learns from Yama, the god of death, the secret of the immortal Self; the Kena asks by whom the mind is directed and recounts the parable of the gods' victory, Indra and Uma revealing that all power belongs to Brahman. The Upanishads are the philosophical culmination of the Vedas and the source of Vedanta's teaching that Atman and Brahman are one. Paramananda's version is valued for its devotional clarity.
